step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram shows Vizio's telemetry and data analytics pipeline on AWS. Smart TVs send telemetry (logs, performance, user data) to Kinesis Data Streams. The stream feeds Kinesis Data Firehose, which delivers all raw data down to an S3 bucket for long-term storage and forwards relevant columns to Redshift for data warehousing. Redshift data is then queried and visualized in QuickSight via its SPICE engine.

graph.name: Vizio Telemetry and Analytics Architecture
graph.notes: Vizio ingests telemetry from millions of connected smart TVs generating billions of events per month using Kinesis, Firehose, S3, Redshift, and QuickSight.

nodes.name: Smart TV
nodes.notes: Millions of connected TVs generating logs, performance telemetry, and user usage data.

nodes.name: Kinesis Data Streams
nodes.notes: Front door to the cloud running an 8-shard pipeline to handle raw data stream ingestion.

nodes.name: Kinesis Firehose
nodes.notes: Pipes schema-less raw data streams directly to long-term storage and data warehouse.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Persistent long-term storage keeping all raw telemetry columns forever.

nodes.name: Redshift
nodes.notes: Columnar data warehouse optimized for aggregating billions of telemetry events.

nodes.name: QuickSight
nodes.notes: Visualization platform utilizing custom SQL queries and the SPICE in-memory database for snappy reporting.

edges.notes: Smart TVs stream logs, performance, and user data to Kinesis Data Streams.
Kinesis streams feed directly into Kinesis Firehose.
Kinesis Firehose dumps the complete, raw telemetry data into S3.
Kinesis Firehose ingests structured subsets of data into Redshift.
Custom SQL queries pull aggregated data from Redshift into QuickSight SPICE datasets.
